correctness.rationale: For every analytic Schwarz function omega fixing zero, w=omega(z), s=|w|<=r, the exact differentiation identity 1+zf''/f'=phi(w)+z omega'(z)*(1+1/[2(1+w)]) holds. Coefficient recurrence (n+1)a_{n+1}=(3/2-n)a_n+a_{n-1}, with alternating sign from n=5, yields Re phi(w)>=phi(-s) through s<=17/50 using the positive polynomial 3/2-7s/2-11s^3/8. Schwarz–Pick applied to omega(z)/z gives |z omega'|<=s+(r^2-s^2)/(1-r^2); the lower envelope K_r(s)=phi(-s)-m_r(s)(1+1/[2(1-s)]) decreases with s on 0<=s<=r<=17/50 and equals H(r) at s=r. Canonical omega(z)=z at z=-r attains equality. H decreases and has rigorous sign-changing rational brackets at 1/3 and 17/50, hence one sharp root R, with H<0 just above it. Complex target has Re phi>0 by boundary argument sin theta+theta/4<pi/2, guaranteeing normalized starlike/univalent functions. At r=0 radial order is 1. All quantifiers and r<=R boundary hold; no extrapolation of radial equality above R.
residual_risks: The 20,000 finite Blaschke tests and 161 coefficient terms are corroboration, not proofs for all Schwarz maps; the analytic sign induction and Schwarz–Pick comparison carry the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The sharp classical convexity radius of a defined and studied Ma–Minda starlike family is a natural geometric invariant: it is the largest centered subdisk on which every normalized image is convex. The theorem determines a full sharp radial order, a unique exact boundary root, and one extremizer for all r<=R. The target-specific alternating coefficient inequality and Schwarz–Pick optimization are substantive, not a textbook substitution or arbitrary narrow parameter slice. It provides a benchmark to distinguish apple-class starlikeness from local classical convexity; it does not extend to r>R or unrelated targets.
residual_risks: The target class is recently introduced and the result is an explicit specialized sharp radius, not a general new method or cross-target classification.
Possible prior generic all-target theorem would also affect independent value; bounded comparisons found none.

limitations: Only the defined apple-like starlike class and r<=R sharp radial identity; no claim of exact inequality for r>R, global univalence beyond known positive-real target, or external certification. Best-of-knowledge originality bounded by stated residuals. Publication is not_ready for public metadata provenance, not because science failed.
